title: Core eventual pair defect zero
statement: Under the hypotheses of finitePresentation_local_map_pair_eventually_defect_zero, there is a stage l ≥ k such that at every later stage the overlap defect is zero in every universal-test descent square.

proof.text: Construct W as the pullback of the two affine open-cover maps and d as localMapPairOverlapDefect. Its source and target are successive native pullbacks of F and G. Register the given finite-presentation and quasi-coherence instances; pullback preserves them (Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_pullback and isQuasicoherent_pullback). The stage scheme is quasi-separated because its map to the affine base is quasi-separated. The intersection of the two affine opens is compact, and its map to Spec R_k is quasi-compact.

At the limit, hr identifies the transported family with the components of the canonical descent morphism obtained by applying toDescentData to delta. Its Hom.comm field gives PairCompatibility. Apply the forward implication of localMapPairOverlapDefect_baseChange_iff to conclude that the pulled defect is zero.

Apply finitePresentation_test_map_zero_eventually to the explicit d on W. The finite-presentation, quasi-coherence and quasi-compactness hypotheses were checked above. Obtain l >= k where its pullback is zero.

For m >= l construct the canonical lift from W times_X X_m to W times_X X_l. The overlapStageMap_comp equation shows its defining pullback square commutes. PullbackComp naturality transports zero along this lift, because native module pullback maps zero to zero. Apply the reverse implication of localMapPairOverlapDefect_baseChange_iff at m. Each square then has its left composite as a common value, proving PairDefectZero at every m >= l.
